st.headline: World’s largest miner unveils US$17.4b plan to double South Australian copper output by 2040
st.teaser: BHP expects global copper demand to grow by 30% by 2040 to more than 45 million tonnes per year.
fullText: MELBOURNE – Top global miner BHP said on Nov 23 it plans to double its South Australian copper production by 2040, as it raises its exposure to the metal expected to drive electrification, with a final investment decision due in the first half of 2027.

BHP plans to spend between US$13.6 billion (S$17.5 billion) and US$17.4 billion to raise production to an estimated 650,000 tonnes a year from its sprawling copper operations in a remote region that it says is the world’s richest source of copper outside Chile.

The plan knits together its Copper South Australia operations at its anchor Olympic Dam copper mine, its Ankata deposit, and the mines gained in its A$9.6 billion (S$8.2 billion) purchase of OZ Minerals in 2023.

“We start from a strong position as the world’s largest copper producer, with a sector-leading growth pathway that can be funded from existing copper cash flows,” Geraldine Slattery, BHP’s head of Australian operations, told investors on a site tour, according to prepared remarks supplied by BHP.
“Copper South Australia is a centrepiece of that growth, contributing around a third of the increase to 2035.”

BHP projected Copper South Australia’s output would grow to rival its share in Escondida, the world’s largest copper mine, by 2040. That would underpin BHP’s goal to produce 2 million tonnes of the metal, or 2.5 million including byproducts, from its global operations by the mid-2030s.
Slattery said BHP expects global copper demand to grow by 30% by 2040 to more than 45 million tonnes per year, driven by electrification, digitalisation and AI demand.
BHP, the world’s largest listed miner, reaped more value from its copper division than from iron ore, its prior mainstay, for the first time in fiscal 2026.
BHP has twice shelved plans in previous decades to develop its rich but technically complex ore assets, citing high costs and commodity downturns.
The operations have proven challenging due to a combination of operational instability, complex metallurgy and external infrastructure constraints such as water and power, UBS said in a note.
As a result, the operations have achieved a low single-digit return on capital employed for many years, reaching only 10% in fiscal 2026 with record-high commodity prices, UBS added.

BHP said it expects block caving, which is a type of bulk mining, and two-stage smelting to underpin significantly lower operating costs. It said phase one, which aims to produce 500,000 tonnes of copper annually by 2035, would have an internal rate of return of 14% to 17%, and capital intensity of US$18,000 to US$23,000 per tonne of copper.

As part of the expansion, BHP plans to roughly double the capacity of its uranium processing plant to 5,000 to 6,000 tonnes a year. It would also boost its gold production by 45% to more than 570,000 troy ounces a year.
BHP’s mines sit within the Gawler Craton, an ancient geological structure formed roughly two billion years ago, in an increasingly arid region on the fringes of Australia’s remote Outback.

The miner uses water from the Great Artesian Basin, which has sparked concerns about overuse from traditional owner groups such as the Arabana people. BHP aims to mitigate its use of the artesian water by using a planned 260-megalitre-a-day seawater desalination plant at Cape Hardy on South Australia’s Spencer Gulf. That water would need to be piped hundreds of kilometres.

The state government is running a tender for the multi-user Northern Water infrastructure project with two global consortia. It is due to make a final investment decision in 2027 , and the first water from the project is targeted for fiscal 2032.
The planned expansion will also require power upgrades to existing electricity transmission infrastructure. REUTERS

cna.headline: India draw feels like a win for New Zealand skipper Latham
cna.teaser: India draw feels like a win for New Zealand skipper Latham
fullText: Nov 23 : New Zealand captain Tom Latham said the draw in the first test against India on Monday felt like a victory given the parlous positions his team were in at various points of the match in Wellington.

India, who posted 720-9 declared in their single innings, were left five wickets short of a victory after a battling rearguard from Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips denied them for almost two sessions on the final day.

That the match remained alive until the fifth day looked highly unlikely after India reduced the home side to 70-5 just after lunch on the opening day before the pitch flattened out and New Zealand posted 368.
"I guess that's one that we've probably got away with," Latham told reporters at Basin Reserve.

"Heading into the third innings, where there's only a couple of results at play, I think (it's great) the way those guys were able to apply themselves and stick to their plans for a long period of time, and ultimately get the draw."

Latham, whose own contribution to the batting was a pair of ducks after being dismissed by Jasprit Bumrah in the first over of each innings, said the draw was particularly important for the race to the World Test Championship (WTC) final.

New Zealand were top of the WTC standings at the start of the test last week only to be overhauled by reigning champions South Africa. Monday's draw means they will slip down another place to third behind Australia.

With the second India test in Christchurch followed by a tour of Australia and a home series against Sri Lanka, however, Latham felt New Zealand still had plenty of time to secure one of the two slots in the final at The Oval in June.
"Draws become important as well," added the opener, who helped New Zealand beat India in 2021 to win the first WTC final.
"It's not necessarily over one series that you've got to play well. It's over a two-year period and it depends on how many games you've got.
"Obviously, we've got more games left than most teams ... (and) hopefully, we'll give ourselves a chance throughout the next couple of months to be in that position."
A single handpicked story that we think you shouldn't miss. Just one a day.

mom.headline: More than 782,000 Singaporean Seniors to Benefit from $1.04 Billion Budget 2026 CPF Top-Up to Boost Retirement Savings
mom.teaser: More than 782,000 eligible Singaporean seniors will receive a CPF top-up of up to $1,500 by 8 December 2026. First announced at Budget 2026, this top-up will support seniors who may face challenges in building their retirement savings.

listening.title: Singapore Pilots Autonomous Shuttles in Punggol
listening.transcript: Singapore is set to pilot new autonomous shuttles in Punggol by the end of this year, aiming to enhance first-and-last-mile connectivity for commuters. Transport authorities highlighted that these driverless vehicles will undergo rigorous safety testing before being integrated into daily transit schedules. Local residents expressed cautious optimism about the initiative, noting that reliable tech could ease peak-hour congestion in suburban towns.

economistArticle.title: Deflating the Bubble: How Much Air Remains in the AI Market?
paras: For over two years, financial markets have been propelled by an unyielding enthusiasm for artificial intelligence. Valuations for tech behemoths soared to astronomical heights on the promise that generative models would fundamentally reshape global commerce. Yet, recent stock market tremors suggest that investors are beginning to suffer from collective exhaustion, questioning whether the vast capital expenditure on data centres and specialised microchips will yield proportionate returns in the near term.

The recent pullback is not merely a transient glitch, but rather an overdue reality check. Wall Street analysts are increasingly scrutinising tech earnings reports for signs of revenue monetization, only to find that commercial adoption remains in its nascent stages. While chipmakers continue to report lucrative revenues, the enterprise software firms expected to convert AI capabilities into recurring subscription fees are struggling to show commensurate growth.

This asymmetry has ignited fears of a classic market correction. Capital allocation has become dangerously concentrated in a handful of megacap tech equities, leaving broader market indices vulnerable to sharp downturns. If the projected productivity gains fail to materialize quickly, the inflated multiples attached to these technology titans could deflate rapidly, triggering wider systemic repercussions.

Moreover, supply chain bottlenecks and staggering power requirements pose formidable physical constraints to continued exponential expansion. Constructing energy-intensive server facilities requires unprecedented grid infrastructure, leading to regulatory delays that could further dampen institutional enthusiasm. Investors who once treated AI investments as a risk-free bet are now recalibrating their risk assessments in response to these structural headwinds.

Ultimately, a moderate retrenchment may prove healthy for the broader economic ecosystem. Stripping away the speculative froth forces technology developers to pivot from grandiose promises to practical, value-generating applications. The market may be troubled today, but a more sober valuation of artificial intelligence could lay the groundwork for sustainable long-term growth.
economistArticle.cn:
两年来，金融市场一直受到对人工智能的不懈热情的推动。科技巨头们的估值升至天文数字，因为市场预期生成式模型将从根本上重塑全球商业。然而，近期股票市场的震荡表明，投资者正开始感到集体疲倦，开始质疑数据中心和专用芯片上的巨额资本支出能否在短期内带来成比例的回报。

最近的回调不仅是一个短暂的小故障，更是一场迟到的现实检验。华尔街分析师正日益审视科技公司的财报，寻找营收变现的迹象，结果却发现商业应用仍处于初级阶段。虽然芯片制造商继续报告丰厚的收入，但那些被预期将人工智能能力转化为持续订阅费的企业软件公司，却难以展现出相匹配的增长。

这种不对称引发了人们对经典市场回调的担忧。资本配置危险地集中在少数超级大盘科技股中，使得更广泛的股票市场指数极易受到剧烈下跌的影响。如果预期的生产力提升不能迅速实现，附着在这些科技巨头身上的膨胀估值倍数可能会迅速缩水，从而引发更广泛的系统性涟漪反应。

此外，供应链瓶颈和惊人的电力需求对持续的指数级扩张构成了严峻的物理制约。建设能源密集型服务器设施需要前所未有的电网基础设施，从而导致监管延误，进一步打击机构投资者的热情。曾经将人工智能投资视为无风险押注的投资者，如今正因这些结构性逆风而重新评估其风险。

归根结底，适度的收缩对更广泛的经济生态系统来说可能是健康的。剥离投机泡沫迫使技术开发人员从宏大的许诺转向务实且能创造价值的实际应用。今天的市场或许动荡不安，但对人工智能更为理性的估值，可能为可持续的长期增长奠定基础。

gems.s: The recent pullback is not merely a transient glitch, but rather an overdue reality check.
gems.why: Uses the contrasting frame 'not merely A, but rather B' alongside metaphors ('transient glitch', 'reality check') to reframe market decline as a necessary corrective rather than an anomaly. 巧妙运用“不仅不是A，反而是一场迟到的B”句型，将市场下跌重新定义为理性的回归，增强论证说服力。

gems.s: Stripping away the speculative froth forces technology developers to pivot from grandiose promises to practical, value-generating applications.
gems.why: Employs vivid imagery ('speculative froth') and dynamic verbs ('strip away', 'pivot') to contrast empty hype ('grandiose promises') with business utility ('value-generating applications'). 通过“剥离泡沫”这一生动比喻与“从虚妄承诺转向实际价值”的对比，鲜明指明了行业发展的正确方向。
